q: 1. The construction of a temporary structure required to support an unsafe structure, is called
explain: Shoring is the provision of temporary supports (shores) to prevent the collapse of an unsafe wall or structure during repairs or nearby excavation.

q: 2. A brick which is half as wide as a full brick, is called
explain: A queen closer is created by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves. It is used to maintain the bond (overlap) at the end of a wall course.

q: 3. In brick masonry, for good bonding
options: all bricks need not be uniform in size
bats must be used in alternate courses only
vertical joints in alternate courses should fall in plumb
cement mortar used must have surkhi as additive
explain: Strong bonding requires that vertical joints do not align across consecutive courses. Having vertical joints 'fall in plumb' (aligning every other course) ensures maximum load distribution.

q: 4. The heading bond is usually used for
explain: A header bond (bricks laid with ends facing out) is used for walls with a thickness of one full brick (roughly 200mm) to provide better transverse strength.

q: 5. The inner section of a cavity wall, is generally known as
explain: A cavity wall consists of two separate walls (leaves) with a gap between them. The inner part is called the 'inner leaf' or 'inner leaf wall'.

q: 6. The type of pointing in which upper side of mortar joints is kept about 12 mm inside the face of the masonry and bottom is kept flushed with face of wall, is
explain: Struck pointing is designed to shed rainwater effectively. The slope created by recessing the top edge allows water to run off the joint rather than sitting on it.

q: 7. Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds
explain: To prevent cracking due to thermal expansion and contraction, long masonry walls must have expansion joints at intervals, typically capped at a maximum of 40 meters.

q: 8. The nominal thickness of the brick wall in mm, is
explain: While a standard modular brick is 190mm long, the 'nominal' thickness includes the mortar joint, bringing the standard wall thickness calculation to 200mm.

q: 9. The exterior corner of wall is known as ...........
explain: In masonry, the external corner of a building or the stones/bricks forming that corner are called quoins.

q: 10. The surface of the wall exposed to weather is called ...........
explain: In masonry, the 'face' is the exterior surface of a wall that is visible and exposed to the weather, while the 'back' is the inner surface.

q: 11. The portion of the wall between the facing and backing of the wall is called ...........
explain: The interior portion of a thick wall, situated between the external facing and internal backing, is filled with 'hearting' (usually rubble or lower-grade brick).

q: 12. The portion of the brick obtained by cutting into two portions longitudinally is called ...........
explain: A queen closer is a brick cut in half along its length. It is used to maintain the bond at the end of a wall (the quoin).

q: 13. A temporary rigid structure having platforms to enable masons to work at different stages of a building, is known as
explain: Scaffolding is a temporary structure used to support a work crew and materials to aid in the construction, maintenance, and repair of buildings.

q: 14. The portion of the brick obtained by cutting it in transverse direction is called ...........
explain: A 'bat' is a piece of brick cut across its width. Common types include half-bats or three-quarter bats.

q: 15. The arrangement made to support an unsafe structure temporarily, is known as
explain: Shoring is the process of temporarily supporting a building, vessel, structure, or trench with shores (props) when in danger of collapse or during alterations.

q: 16. The portion of a brick which is cut at one corner such that at one end its width is half of that of a full brick is called ...........
explain: A king closer is formed by cutting off a triangular piece from one corner, reaching from the middle of the header to the middle of the stretcher.

q: 17. The masonry with stone having chisel-dressed on all beds and joints to be true and square giving perfectly vertical & horizontal joint is called
explain: Ashlar masonry uses finely dressed stones with extremely thin joints, creating a very smooth and formal appearance compared to rubble masonry.

q: 18. The brick which is cut such that at one end half the width is maintained and at the other end full width is maintained is called ...........
explain: A beveled closer has one full-length stretcher face, but the width at one end is cut to be half the width of the brick.

q: 19. The brick which is cut such that no longer face is full and the other longer face is small in length is called ...........
explain: A mitred closer is cut at an angle (usually 45 to 60 degrees) along its length, so one stretcher face is shorter than the other.

q: 20. The structure on which arch rests in called
explain: The abutment is the end support of an arch or bridge that resists the lateral thrust of the arch.

q: 21. The overlapping of bricks or stones in masonry is called ...........
explain: Bonding is the arrangement of bricks or stones to ensure they overlap, preventing continuous vertical joints and distributing loads throughout the wall.

q: 22. Numbers of bricks required for one cubic meter masonry wall as per Nepal standard
explain: Standard practice in Nepal estimates approximately 560 bricks per cubic meter for traditional brick masonry including mortar joints.

q: 23. A groove provided on the underside of projecting elements such as cornices, copings such that rain water can be discharged clear of the wall surface is called ...........
explain: Throating is a small groove on the underside of a sill or coping that prevents rainwater from running back onto the wall, protecting it from dampness.

q: 24. Brick wall could fail due to
options: rupture along a vertical joint in poorly bonded walls
explain: Brick walls can fail through various mechanisms including compression (crushing), shear, or poor interlocking (bond) between bricks.

q: 25. A brick or stone put in position in the masonry such that its length is perpendicular to the face of the wall is known as ...........
explain: A header is a brick laid so that only its smallest face (end) is visible on the surface of the wall.

q: 26. Cement sand mortar preferred in load bearing wall is
explain: For load-bearing walls, a 1:6 cement-to-sand ratio provides a balanced strength that allows for minor settlements without brittle failure.

q: 27. A brick or stone put in position in the masonry such that its length is parallel to the face of the wall is known as ...........
explain: A stretcher is a brick laid with its longest side (length) parallel to the face of the wall.

q: 28. The brick laid with its breadth parallel to the face of a wall, is known as
explain: A header is a brick laid so that its end (breadth) is visible on the face of the wall.

q: 29. In random rubble masonry ...........
options: the stones are neatly dressed and laid in courses
the stones are neatly dressed but not built to courses
the stone are either not dressed or roughly dressed and may be coursed or uncoursed
the stones are not dressed and are laid without mortar
explain: Random rubble masonry uses stones of irregular shapes and sizes, which are roughly dressed or not dressed at all, and can be laid in layers (coursed) or at random.

q: 30. The main purpose of cavity wall is
explain: Cavity walls utilize an air gap to prevent moisture travel, provide thermal resistance, and act as a sound barrier.

q: 31. Cavity wall
options: prevent dampness from entering the building
have lesser dead load for given wall thickness
provide better insulation for heat & sound
explain: Cavity walls are multifunctional: they block capillary moisture, reduce building weight, and improve the indoor climate through air-gap insulation.

q: 32. A low height wall constructed along edge of the roof is called ...........
explain: A parapet wall is a low wall built at the edge of a roof or balcony for safety and to hide the roof surface.

q: 33. Cavity wall provided with
explain: The defining feature of a cavity wall is the continuous air space (gap) between the inner and outer leaves.

q: 34. The tool used by the masons to check the verticality of walls is ...........
explain: A plumb bob is a weighted string used to determine a perfectly vertical line (plumb) for brickwork or stone walls.

q: 35. Which of the following wall is not designed for taking lateral load
explain: Gravity walls rely on their own weight to resist lateral earth pressure, but unlike buttress or counterfort walls, they aren't 'designed' with specific lateral reinforcement components.

q: 36. The cut or broken portion of brick is called
explain: A brick bat is a piece of brick with one or more ends cut off, usually across the width.

q: 37. The part of brick cut from a whole brick to maintain the bond in such a way that its one long face remains uncut is known as
explain: A closer is a portion of a brick used to close the bond at the end of a course, such as a queen closer or king closer.

q: 38. The bricks arranged projecting in alternate courses for the purpose of bonding future masonry work is called ...........
explain: Toothing is the process of leaving bricks projecting from a wall so that another wall can be bonded into it later.

q: 39. The portion of brick obtained by cutting a brick lengthwise into two directions is known as
explain: A queen closer is made by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves, often used next to a quoin header.

q: 40. A projected stone in masonry wall provided to serve as a support to joist or truss is known as ...
explain: A corbel is a stone or brick projecting from a wall to support a heavy load, such as a beam, joist, or truss.

q: 41. The slenderness ratio for masonry walls should not be more
explain: For safety against buckling, masonry codes typically limit the slenderness ratio (height to thickness) to 20 for cement mortar walls.

q: 42. A projected ornamental course near the top of the wall or near the junction of the wall and ceiling is known as ...
explain: A cornice is a decorative horizontal molding that crowns a building or furniture element, typically found at the top of a wall.

q: 43. The covering on the exposed top of a wall is called ...........
explain: Coping is a protective cap or cover (usually stone or brick) on the top of a wall to shed water and prevent moisture from entering the wall.

q: 44. In brick masonry, the bond produced by laying alternate headers and stretchers in each course is known as
explain: Flemish bond consists of alternate headers and stretchers in every course.

q: 45. A brick which has one or two rounded edges and used to obtain rounded corners in the wall is called .......
explain: A bull nose brick is manufactured with one or more rounded edges, used for aesthetics or to prevent sharp corners on walls.

q: 46. In Nepal, the generally used method of bond in masonry wall of brickwork is
explain: English bond is widely preferred for its superior strength, consisting of alternate courses of headers and stretchers.

q: 47. Stretcher bond is possible only in ...........
explain: Since stretcher bond only shows the long face of the brick, it can only be used for walls that are half-a-brick thick (partition walls).

q: 48. The type of bond provided in brick masonry for carrying heavy loads
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond in brick masonry and is used for structures subjected to heavy loads.

q: 49. The bond which consists of alternate courses of headers and stretchers is known as ..........
explain: English bond is considered the strongest bond, consisting of one course of headers followed by one course of stretchers.

q: 50. The stretcher bond in brick masonry can be used only when the wall is of
explain: Stretcher bond lacks internal ties across the wall thickness, making it suitable only for partition walls (half-brick thick).
